journal_article.person_policy: Third person preferred; first-person plural ('we') permitted sparingly for methodological choices and contributions. Avoid singular 'I' and reader-addressing 'you'.

tense_policy.abstract_methods_results: past tense for completed experiments and observations
tense_policy.established_facts_figures_tables: present tense for general truths, equations, and referring to figures/tables ('Fig. 1 shows')
tense_policy.conclusions_implications: present tense with appropriate epistemic hedging

avoid_patterns: promotional hype (groundbreaking, revolutionary, unprecedented, game-changing, very good, super)
colloquial contractions (don't, can't, won't, isn't, it's)
vague intensifiers (very, really, quite, a lot of, lots of, huge, awesome)
Chinglish openers (with the rapid development of, nowadays, in recent years more and more)
journal_article.citation_and_ref_style: Preserve exact citation format ([1], \cite{}, Author et al., Year) and figure/table prefixes (Fig., Table, Eq.).

thesis_dissertation.tone: formal, systematic, rigorous, transparent about scope and limitations
thesis_dissertation.person_policy: Impersonal or institutional third person ('this study', '本文', '本研究') preferred; avoid colloquial first-person.
avoid_patterns: oral fillers (众所周知, 毫无疑问, 显而易见 without citation, 非常大, 特别好)
unsupported absolute claims (完全解决, 彻底消除, 首次证明 without evidence)
thesis_dissertation.citation_and_ref_style: Preserve chapter numbering, equation numbering, and GB/T 7714 or target university citation format.

grant_proposal.label_zh: 基金申请书（Grant Proposal / NSFC / NIH）
grant_proposal.tone: persuasive yet scientifically grounded, structured, clear gap-to-objective logic
grant_proposal.person_policy: First-person plural ('we', '本项目', '申请团队') appropriate for research plan and preliminary work.
avoid_patterns: overpromising guaranteed outcomes where feasibility is conditional
ambiguity between completed preliminary results and proposed future tasks
grant_proposal.citation_and_ref_style: Preserve exact preliminary data metrics, funding codes, and reference numbers.

peer_review_rebuttal.person_policy: First-person plural ('we thank the reviewer', 'we have revised') standard.

tense_policy.revisions_made: present perfect ('we have added', 'we have clarified')

avoid_patterns: defensive or dismissive phrasing ('the reviewer misunderstood', 'obviously')
unfulfilled promises without concrete line/page/section pointers
excessive flattery that obscures technical answers
peer_review_rebuttal.citation_and_ref_style: Preserve exact reviewer comment IDs (e.g., R1-C2), page/line numbers, and quoted revised text.

bilingual_abstract.tone: high information density, self-contained, parallel semantic alignment between ZH and EN
bilingual_abstract.person_policy: Third person or concise 'we' in EN; impersonal ('本文', '本研究') in ZH.
avoid_patterns: word-for-word literal translation from Chinese topic-comment structure into awkward English
introducing claims, numbers, or abbreviations in one language absent from the other
bilingual_abstract.citation_and_ref_style: Align every numerical result, unit, sample size, and key term strictly across ZH and EN.
